note: Documents why the GuardDuty-native half of security-posture-dashboard (and eks-security-dashboard's GuardDuty widget) could not be exercised with a safe synthetic method, unlike the Security Hub half.
finding_1: aws guardduty create-sample-findings generates real GuardDuty findings (confirmed via aws guardduty list-findings - real, new finding IDs each time) and those findings DO eventually appear in Security Hub via the standard product integration (confirmed in this same session's aws-remediation-orchestrator proof, and again here after a several-minute delay).
finding_2: Sample findings never triggered GuardDuty's own native EventBridge event (source: aws.guardduty, detail-type: GuardDuty Finding). Verified with a minimal, isolated probe rule matching only {"source":["aws.guardduty"]} (no detail-type filter) attached to a throwaway log group - zero deliveries across multiple sample-finding generations and several minutes of waiting, despite the same probe pattern working instantly for real Security Hub Findings-Imported events later in this session.
attempted_workaround: aws events put-events with Source=aws.guardduty and a schema-accurate synthetic detail payload was refused: NotAuthorizedForSourceException: Not authorized for the source. EventBridge does not allow PutEvents to spoof AWS-service-reserved source names, so this event path cannot be safely synthesized the way Security Hub's BatchImportFindings allows.
conclusion: The GuardDuty-native EventBridge path in this repo's dashboards can only be validated with genuine (non-sample) GuardDuty findings, e.g. real reconnaissance/compromise activity or AWS's separate 'Threat List' test mechanism, neither of which is safe or appropriate to trigger for a repo test. This is a real, confirmed limitation of GuardDuty's sample-finding feature, not a defect in the dashboard modules.
